INSIGHT_WORKSPACE_ID.description: Server-side Insight schema / workspace identifier forwarded into the ?objectSchemaId=<value> query-string filter on GET /rest/insight/1.0/iql/objects so the dispatcher only walks one Insight object schema per agent run. Optional; empty / blank walks every object the operator's token can see across every schema (the dispatcher's token scope still applies). Forwarded verbatim — Insight accepts both numeric schema ids (e.g. objectSchemaId=42) and the literal schema key (e.g. objectSchemaId=ITSM) in the objectSchemaId slot depending on tenant configuration so the executor doesn't second-guess operator-supplied workspace ids. When INSIGHT_IQL is blank and INSIGHT_OBJECT_TYPE is blank we also fall back to composing an objectSchema = <workspace> predicate into the IQL so the walk is still scoped on tenants where objectSchemaId isn't enforced at the URL tier. Whitespace is trimmed.

INSIGHT_IQL.description: Operator-supplied Insight Query Language (IQL) predicate forwarded verbatim into the ?iql=<value> query-string parameter on GET /rest/insight/1.0/iql/objects. Optional; empty / blank falls back to the composed predicate built from INSIGHT_OBJECT_TYPE / INSIGHT_WORKSPACE_ID (so leaving all three blank walks every object the token can see). Free-form IQL — e.g. '"Owner" = "ops" AND created > "2026-01-01"' or 'Status IN ("Live", "Stage")' or 'objectType = "Server" AND "Environment" = "Production"'. When INSIGHT_OBJECT_TYPE is ALSO supplied the two predicates compose into objectType = "<type>" AND (<INSIGHT_IQL>) so the operator's IQL is preserved under parentheses and never silently overrides the type filter. Whitespace is trimmed.

INSIGHT_OBJECT_TYPE.description: Optional per-type narrowing knob composed into the IQL as an objectType = "<value>" predicate. Empty / blank walks every object type in the schema (subject to INSIGHT_IQL / INSIGHT_WORKSPACE_ID narrowing). When supplied the value is double-quoted into the IQL so object types with spaces (e.g. 'Network Device' / 'Operating System' / 'Service Contract') round-trip correctly. When INSIGHT_IQL is ALSO supplied the two compose into objectType = "<type>" AND (<INSIGHT_IQL>) so the type filter never silently overrides the operator's IQL. Whitespace is trimmed.

name: jira_insight
title: Atlassian Insight (Assets)
description: Atlassian Insight (Assets) asset-inventory importer. Pulls Insight / Jira Service Management Assets objects from an Atlassian tenant via the Insight v1 REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Atlassian Insight (now branded 'Jira Service Management Assets') is the CMDB Atlassian customers use to track servers, network gear, applications, contracts, and just about any other typed asset they can model into an object schema, so this executor is the CMDB-class feed Faraday operators correlate the EDR / EASM / vuln-scanner agents' findings against to confirm an exposed host is a known managed Insight object. Each Insight object becomes one Faraday host (the first IP-shaped attribute value — matched by IP_RE against the flat list of attributes[*].objectAttributeValues[*].value / displayValue projections — projects onto host.ip; loopback / 0.0.0.0 / ::1 are explicitly skipped and the executor falls back to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel when nothing usable is found; the label / objectKey / name projection lands on host.hostnames with any FQDN-shaped attribute values appended as additional pivots; the first MAC-shaped attribute value lands on host.mac; and the first OS-keyword-shaped attribute value joins onto host.os). The asset itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [ASSET-INVENTORY] engine prefix so the data lands in the Faraday workspace alongside the other CMDB-class feeds (Axonius, Device42, Fleet, runZero, Armis, Jamf Pro). Endpoint used: GET /rest/insight/1.0/iql/objects?iql=<IQL>&page=N&resultPerPage=50(&objectSchemaId=...) (the canonical Insight v1 IQL object walk; returns the envelope {objectEntries: [...], objectTypeAttributes: [...], totalFilterCount: N, startIndex: K, toIndex: K+M, pageObject: P, pageSize: M, iql: '...'} with each objectEntries record carrying id, label, objectKey, name, avatar, objectType ({id, name, type}), created, updated, plus attributes — a list of {id, objectTypeAttributeId, objectAttributeValues: [{value, displayValue, searchValue, referencedType, referencedObject}]} records that hold the operator-modelled attribute payload). INSIGHT_WORKSPACE_ID is forwarded as a server-side ?objectSchemaId=<value> query-string filter; INSIGHT_OBJECT_TYPE is composed into the IQL as an objectType = "<value>" predicate; INSIGHT_IQL is forwarded verbatim into the ?iql=<value> query parameter (when INSIGHT_OBJECT_TYPE is also supplied the two compose into objectType = "<type>" AND (<INSIGHT_IQL>) so the operator's IQL is preserved under parentheses). Pagination is page-based via page (1-indexed) + resultPerPage; walked page-by-page (page += 1 per request) until len(objectEntries) < resultPerPage or INSIGHT_PAGES (env-only override, default 5, clamped to [1, 50]) is reached; resultPerPage is fixed at 50 (Insight's documented default). Severity is always info because Insight hits are CMDB inventory entries, not vulnerability findings — operators correlate against the other agents' findings via the Insight-Id / Insight-Key / Insight-Workspace / Insight-ObjectType / Insight-ObjectTypeId / Insight-Created / Insight-Updated refs. Auth: Atlassian's REST API uses HTTP Basic Authentication with the user's email as the username and an Atlassian-issued API token as the password (Cloud tenants generate the token at https://id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens; on-prem Server / DC tenants accept the user's actual password or a PAT issued from the user profile). The dispatcher carries the credentials in the standard Authorization: Basic <base64(JIRA_USER:JIRA_API_TOKEN)> header on every /rest/insight/1.0/ call. JIRA_HOST is the operator's Jira / JSM tenant host (e.g. mycorp.atlassian.net); on-prem deployments are tolerated and https:// is added automatically when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Tags: [jira_insight, asset-inventory, object].
